setup: Set the bar at mid-chest height in the rack
Bar on your upper back, not your neck
Step back, feet shoulder width, toes slightly out
execution: Breathe in, brace, then sit down
Sink until hips are just below knees, heels down
Stand up with hips and chest rising together
faults: Hips rising faster than the chest
Lower back rounding at the bottom

notes: Squat inside a rack with the safety arms set just below the lowest point the bar reaches.
Practise lowering a light bar onto the safety arms so you know how to bail out of a failed rep.
A spotter is optional and does not replace safety arms. If you use one, agree the signals before the set.
Only go as deep as you can with heels down and your lower back holding its position.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Bodyweight squat
regressions.reason: Learns the pattern and depth with no load.

regressions.name: Goblet squat
regressions.reason: A load held in front makes an upright torso easier to find.

regressions.name: Box squat
regressions.reason: The box gives a consistent depth target.

progressions.name: Paused back squat
progressions.reason: A pause at the bottom removes the bounce and builds control.

progressions.name: Front squat
progressions.reason: More upright torso and more quad demand; needs more wrist, ankle and upper-back mobility.

substitutions.name: Hack squat
substitutions.reason: Same squat pattern on a guided path; no rack or spotter needed.

substitutions.name: Leg press
substitutions.reason: Trains quads and glutes without a bar on the back.

substitutions.name: Smith machine squat
substitutions.reason: Fixed bar path with built-in catches. Loads are not comparable with a free bar.

substitutions.name: Front squat
substitutions.reason: Same pattern with the bar in front; more upright.

substitutions.name: Bulgarian split squat
substitutions.reason: One leg at a time with much lighter loads.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view, figure facing right, camera at hip height, whole body in frame. Rack uprights optional, drawn behind the figure.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall. Knees and hips straight but not forced back. Bar on the upper back directly over mid-foot. Hands just outside the shoulders, elbows pointing down and slightly back. Feet flat.

keyPositions.label: Halfway
keyPositions.describe: Hips moving back and down while the knees move forward over the toes. Bar still over mid-foot. Heels down. Spine neutral.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Hip crease just below the top of the knee (thigh slightly past parallel). Shins and torso at similar forward angles. Heels flat. Lower back neutral, chest up, gaze forward. Bar still over mid-foot.

guideBrief.barPath: Vertical line over mid-foot; drift ≤ 3% of body height
emphasise: Bar stays over mid-foot all the way down and up
Knees travel forward over the toes, not inward
Hips and chest rise at the same rate
doNotShow: Depth past where the back stays neutral

sources.title: Myer GD et al. (2014) The back squat: a proposed assessment of functional deficits and technical factors that limit performance. Strength Cond J 36(6):4-27
sources.supports: cues.setup[3]; cues.execution[0-3]; cues.faults[0-3]; guideBrief.keyPositions[2] (depth, shin and torso angle, heels down, gaze)

uncertain.note: Approximate drawing targets worked out from the cited depth and shin/torso guidance. Not measured data and not a form standard. Trunk lean varies with bar position and body proportions.
Safety-arm and spotter advice is standard gym practice. Neither cited source covers it.
